headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure improvements from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers, by requiring them to pay for increased generating capacity.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocacy groups, environmental groups, some state senators/delegates (e.g., Sen. Louise Lucas, Gov. Spanberger).
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users, utility companies.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill, SB 253 (similar in intent to HB 1393), aims to make data centers pay for their own electrical substations and capacity costs, potentially saving residential customers over $65 annually. This legislation is part of a broader effort to address rising energy costs and ensure data centers do not drive up expenses for families.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing crucial data for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, Del. Elizabeth Guzman, Del. Shelly Simonds, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, including SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This legislation aims to provide transparency and better data for water supply planning, especially as data centers can use millions of gallons daily.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high-energy use facilities, including noise profiles for nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residential groups, environmental advocates, Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: Virginia's new law, including HB 153, requires developers of large data centers (100 MW or more) to conduct site assessments, including noise studies for homes and schools within 500 feet. While it mandates studies and allows localities to assess other impacts like water and agriculture, it does not set statewide noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local authorities.
